2027-07-20.title: Elijah the Prophet · Tuesday of the ninth week after Pentecost
readings: These are only a shadow of what is to come, but the substance belongs to Christ
“Elijah has come”: the question of the disciples as they came down from the mountain
2027-07-20.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the Ninth Sunday after Pentecost. The Panchangam keeps today the memory of Elijah the Prophet (ഏലിയാ നിബിയാ). Nibiya is the Syriac word for prophet. Elijah is one of the prophets of the Old Covenant whom the Panchangam remembers this month, with Aaron, Daniel and Ezekiel. The Panchangam gives the readings of the weekday only.
2027-07-20.verse: Elijah is indeed coming first to restore all things.
theo: Peter, James and John are coming down the mountain, and their heads are still full of what they have seen: the Lord shining like light, and with him Moses and Elijah, “who were talking with Jesus.” Jesus tells them to say nothing “until after the Son of Man had risen from the dead,” and they keep the matter to themselves, “questioning what this rising from the dead could mean.” Then comes the question that has been burning in them: “Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?” The scribes were reading the prophet Malachi: “Lo, I will send you the prophet Elijah before the great and terrible day of the Lord comes. He will turn the hearts of parents to their children and the hearts of children to their parents.” They had just seen Elijah on the mountain. Why was he gone again? Jesus answers in two steps. First: “Elijah is indeed coming first to restore all things.” The promise stands. Then: “But I tell you that Elijah has come, and they did to him whatever they pleased, as it is written about him.” Elijah has come in the person of John the Baptist, who, as the angel told Zechariah, would go before the Lord “with the spirit and power of Elijah.” And the way of the forerunner prepares the way of the Lord: they did to John whatever they pleased, and so the Son of Man “is to go through many sufferings and be treated with contempt.”

Who was Elijah, and why does the Church keep his memory in the season of Pentecost? He appears suddenly in the First Book of Kings, “the Tishbite, of Tishbe in Gilead,” announcing a drought in the days of King Ahab. He is fed first by ravens, then by a poor widow of Zarephath, whose jar of meal “was not emptied, neither did the jug of oil fail, according to the word of the Lord.” On Mount Carmel he stands alone against the prophets of Baal and asks the people the question that he asks still: “How long will you go limping with two different opinions? If the Lord is God, follow him; but if Baal, then follow him.” Fire falls and the people fall on their faces. Then Elijah climbs to the top of Carmel, bows with his face between his knees, and sends his servant to look at the sea, seven times. At the seventh time the servant says: “Look, a little cloud no bigger than a person's hand is rising out of the sea.” In July in Kerala, when the whole land waits for the rain and listens to it on the tiles, we know exactly what that cloud is. St James adds a word for ordinary believers: “Elijah was a human being like us, and he prayed fervently that it might not rain, and for three years and six months it did not rain on the earth. Then he prayed again, and the heaven gave rain and the earth yielded its harvest.”

The same prophet then sits exhausted under a broom tree and begs to die: “It is enough; now, O Lord, take away my life, for I am no better than my ancestors.” The great prophet is a person like us. And God does not answer with a speech. An angel touches him and says: “Get up and eat.” A second time: “Get up and eat, otherwise the journey will be too much for you.” “He got up, and ate and drank; then he went in the strength of that food forty days and forty nights to Horeb the mount of God.” There, God is not in the wind, nor the earthquake, nor the fire, but in “a sound of sheer silence.” The Fathers saw in the cake and the jar of water a sign of the bread that sustains the pilgrim, and the Church gives the Holy Qurbono to the dying as food for the last journey. The Second Book of Kings tells that Elijah went up in a whirlwind, with a chariot of fire, and on the mountain of the Transfiguration he appears again, to listen to the Son.

Today's Epistle gives the key. Paul tells the Colossians not to let anyone judge them in matters of food and drink, festivals, new moons or sabbaths: “These are only a shadow of what is to come, but the substance belongs to Christ.” Paul is not despising the feasts of Israel, which the same Paul calls gifts that belong to Israel (Romans 9:4); he is telling Gentile believers not to let any human group make them anxious about what Christ has already fulfilled. The prophets, too, are a shadow, a light thrown ahead by the one who is coming. The voice at the Transfiguration says of Jesus: “Listen to him!” and then, “they saw no one with them any more, but only Jesus.” We honour Elijah, we pray with him, and we learn courage from him; but we follow the one to whom Moses and Elijah pointed, “the head, from whom the whole body, nourished and held together by its ligaments and sinews, grows with a growth that is from God.” Let us ask the Lord to give us the courage of Elijah to choose, the humility of Elijah to rest and to eat what God provides, and the stillness of Elijah to hear a sound of sheer silence.
outline: Ask: where in my life am I still going limping between two opinions?
Malachi's promise; Elijah has come in John the Baptist, and the forerunner shares the Lord's fate.
Point 2 · Prayer and the little cloud
Carmel, the drought and the rain; Elijah is a human being like us.
Despair under the broom tree; the bread of the journey; the sound of sheer silence.

live: Name one habit or divided loyalty in your life, and make one clear decision this week to follow the Lord in it.
Pray today with persistence, as Elijah did, for something good that you are still waiting for, and for the farmers and families who depend on this monsoon.
If you are weary or discouraged, rest, eat, and then take up the journey; and if you can, receive the Holy Qurbono this week as food for the way.
2027-07-20.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you spoke with Moses and Elijah on the holy mountain, and the Father said of you, Listen to him. We thank you for the prophet Elijah, who stood alone for the living God, who prayed that the rain might come, and whom you strengthened with bread on the way. Give us the courage to choose you without dividing our hearts, the perseverance to pray when the heavens seem closed, and the humility to rise and eat when we are weary. Let us not be led by shadows, but hold fast to you, the head from whom the whole body grows with a growth that is from God. Through the prayers of the prophet Elijah, bless the farmers and the fields in this season of rain. You live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: Elijah went in the strength of the food the angel gave him forty days to the mount of God; in the Holy Qurbono the Lord himself gives us the bread of life, the true food for the long journey, and the Church sends the Qurbono also to the dying as the bread of their last road.
conn: Malachi 4:5–6 promises Elijah before the day of the Lord; Luke 1:17: John will go before the Lord “with the spirit and power of Elijah”; Matthew 17:10–13 records the same conversation after the Transfiguration.
James 5:17–18: Elijah “was a human being like us” and his prayer closed and opened the heavens; 1 Kings 18:42–45 is the little cloud rising from the sea.
1 Kings 19:5–8: “Get up and eat”; John 6:51: “I am the living bread that came down from heaven”; the Church's viaticum is the Holy Qurbono given for the last journey.
fathers: Elijah's long fast was the beginning of his ascent: by fasting and prayer he was lifted above earthly things, and the spirit that is strengthened by fasting is made ready to see God (On Elijah and Fasting, in substance).

John is called Elijah, not because he is the same person but because he has the same spirit and task: both stood alone against the powerful, both called the people back to the Lord, and both lived by simplicity (Homilies on Matthew, in substance).
magis: Elijah, the father of the prophets, is the one in whom the prophetic tradition of Israel is gathered: he teaches the people to turn their hearts to the living God and shows what prayer is when the whole person stands before the Lord (in substance).

Fire symbolises the transforming energy of the acts of the Holy Spirit; in Elijah's prayer on Mount Carmel, fire from heaven consumed the sacrifice, and the Spirit comes as fire on the Apostles at Pentecost (in substance).
John the Baptist is the one sent to go before the Lord in the spirit and power of Elijah; in him the Spirit completes the work of the prophets (in substance).

quick: Coming down from the mountain, the disciples ask why Elijah must come first; Jesus answers that Elijah has come, in John the Baptist.
Elijah stood alone on Mount Carmel, prayed for rain, and was fed with bread on his journey to Horeb.
Paul says that festivals and sabbaths are a shadow of what is to come, but the substance belongs to Christ.
2027-07-20.action: Choose one decision this week that settles a divided loyalty, and pray for rain for the farmers.
2027-07-20.question: Where am I still limping between two opinions, and what is the one thing I need to choose?

family.explain: Elijah was a prophet who loved God very much. When there was no rain for a long time, he prayed, and a tiny cloud, as small as a hand, rose from the sea. Soon there was a big rain! When Elijah was tired and sad, an angel gave him bread and water and said: Get up and eat. God also feeds us with the Holy Qurbono. And on the mountain, when Jesus shone, Elijah was there with Moses, but then the disciples saw only Jesus, because Jesus is the one we follow.
family.intention: We pray for farmers and for all who wait for rain, and for those who feel tired or sad.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one small thing I can pray for with all my heart this week?”

illus: In a hill village in Idukki, the monsoon came late one year and the paddy seedlings in the terraces turned yellow. After the Sunday Qurbana the vicar asked everyone to pray for rain. An old widow who lived at the edge of the village, whose own small field had been dry for three weeks, went home and opened the west window of her kitchen. Every evening, at the hour of the Angelus, she stood there and said, quietly, that she was only watching for the small cloud. Her neighbours teased her gently. On the ninth evening a grey bank came over the ridge, and by midnight the whole village could hear rain on the tin roofs. The next morning she did not say that she had brought the rain. She said that she had learned to look in the right direction, and to go on looking. The farmers of that hill still say, when the sky is slow to open: Let us go and watch for the small cloud.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you spoke with Elijah on the mountain and fed him on the way. Hear our prayer for the rain and for all our needs, and let us follow only you. Amen.
share: How long will you go limping with two different opinions? (1 Kings 18:21). Where am I divided?
Get up and eat, otherwise the journey will be too much for you (1 Kings 19:7). What feeds me for the journey?
These are only a shadow of what is to come, but the substance belongs to Christ (Colossians 2:17). What am I still holding on to that is only a shadow?
interc: For the Church, that like Elijah she may stand firmly for the living God.
For farmers and all who depend on the rain, for good harvests and safe homes in this monsoon.
For those who are tired, discouraged or alone, that the Lord may send them bread for the way.
For parents and children, that their hearts may be turned to one another.
For the dying, that they may be fed with the bread of life for the last journey.

term: The Syriac word for prophet, from the same root as the Hebrew navi. The Syriac calendar remembers the prophets of the Old Covenant by this title: Elijah Nibiya is the prophet Elijah, Daniel Nibiya is the prophet Daniel.
kidsaint: The prophet and the little cloud

Elijah was a prophet who loved God, and he prayed that rain would stop and that it would start again. Ravens brought him bread, and a poor widow shared the last of her flour with him; God made her flour and oil last until the rain came. After a long dry time, Elijah told his servant to look at the sea. Seven times he looked. At last he saw a tiny cloud, as small as a hand, and soon the sky turned black and the rain poured down! Lesson: pray and keep on praying; a tiny cloud can become a great rain.

homily: Dear friends, in today's Gospel the disciples are coming down the mountain after seeing Jesus shining, with Moses and Elijah beside him. They ask: Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first? Jesus answers: Elijah is indeed coming first to restore all things. But I tell you that Elijah has come, and they did to him whatever they pleased (Mark 9:12–13). He means John the Baptist, who came in the spirit and power of Elijah (Luke 1:17).

Who was Elijah? A prophet who stood alone for the living God. On Mount Carmel he asked the people: How long will you go limping with two different opinions? If the Lord is God, follow him (1 Kings 18:21). He prayed fervently, and after a long drought he saw a little cloud no bigger than a person's hand rising out of the sea (1 Kings 18:44). In these monsoon days we know what that cloud means. St James says that Elijah was a human being like us (James 5:17). He also became tired and sad, and God sent him bread and water with the words: Get up and eat, otherwise the journey will be too much for you (1 Kings 19:7).

St Paul tells the Colossians that festivals, new moons and sabbaths are only a shadow of what is to come, but the substance belongs to Christ (Colossians 2:17). The prophets, too, are lights thrown ahead by the one who is coming. When the disciples looked up on the mountain, they saw no one with them any more, but only Jesus (Mark 9:8). We honour Elijah, but we follow Jesus, the head of the body.
Let us ask the Lord for Elijah's courage to choose, his persistence in prayer and his humility to eat the bread God gives. Amen.
kids: Children, do you know what Elijah did when the land was dry and there was no rain? He prayed and prayed, and he sent his servant to look at the sea. Seven times! At last the servant saw a tiny cloud, as small as a hand. And soon there was a big rain, just as in our monsoon! Elijah teaches us to keep praying and not to give up. And when Elijah was tired, an angel gave him bread and said, Get up and eat. God gives us strength for our journey, too.

intro: Theme: “they saw no one with them any more, but only Jesus.”
On Tuesday of the ninth week after Pentecost, the memory of Elijah the Prophet: Elijah has come, the prayer for rain, the bread for the journey, and the shadow and the substance.

sub: Elijah has come in John the Baptist.
The forerunner shares the Lord's fate.
q: Lo, I will send you the prophet Elijah before the great and terrible day of the Lord comes.
With the spirit and power of Elijah he will go before him, to turn the hearts of parents to their children,
points.apply: Ask the Lord to turn the hearts in your own family towards one another.

sub: How long will you go limping?
q: How long will you go limping with two different opinions? If the Lord is God, follow him; but if Baal, then follow him.
Elijah was a human being like us, and he prayed fervently that it might not rain, and for three years and six months it did not rain on the earth.
points.apply: Pray persistently this week for one good thing you are waiting for.

q: Get up and eat, otherwise the journey will be too much for you.
I am the living bread that came down from heaven. Whoever eats of this bread will live forever; and the bread that I will give for the life of the world is my flesh.
points.apply: When you are weary, rest and eat, and receive the Holy Qurbono as food for the way.

q: The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your own people; you shall heed such a prophet.
Suddenly when they looked around, they saw no one with them any more, but only Jesus.
points.apply: Put down one thing you cling to that is only a shadow, and hold fast to Christ.

concl: Elijah teaches us to choose, to pray with persistence and to eat the bread God gives.
All the prophets point ahead; the substance is Christ, the head of the body.
2027-07-20.resolve: Choose the Lord, pray without giving up, eat the bread for the way, and follow Jesus alone.
